modules.name: main
modules.responsibility: CLI entry point: parse mount arguments, initialize the filesystem, register FUSE operations table, and enter the libfuse3 event loop.

modules.name: filesystem
modules.responsibility: Top-level in-memory filesystem state container. Owns the inode table, directory tree, and extended attributes store. All FUSE operation implementations delegate here through a single RwLock-protected instance.

modules.name: inode
modules.responsibility: Inode allocation, deallocation, and attribute management. Defines Inode struct with metadata (mode, uid, gid, size, timestamps, nlink) and the per-inode data buffer (Vec<u8> for regular files, empty for dirs/symlinks).

modules.name: directory
modules.responsibility: Directory entry management: mapping directory inode → set of (name, child_inode) pairs. Supports lookup, add_entry, remove_entry, and readdir iteration.

modules.name: xattr
modules.responsibility: Extended attributes store: per-inode HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>. Provides getxattr, setxattr, listxattr, removexattr operations with size and namespace validation.

modules.name: symlink
modules.responsibility: Symlink target storage and retrieval. Each symlink inode stores a target path string. Exposes readlink (resolve) and symlink (create) helpers.

modules.name: path
modules.responsibility: Path resolution utilities: validate paths, split into components, resolve parent directory, check for conflicts, and enforce naming constraints (no empty names, no '/' in names, max component length).

modules.name: permissions
modules.responsibility: Basic permission checking: owner/group/other read/write/execute bits against caller uid/gid. Used by open, create, mkdir, unlink, rename, chmod, and getattr (for access decisions).

data_model.Root inode: Inode 1 is always the root directory `/`. Created at filesystem init, never deleted.
data_model.Inode lifecycle: Inodes are allocated sequentially (monotonically increasing u64). Freed inodes are NOT reused — this simplifies concurrency and avoids ABA issues.
data_model.File data: Regular file content is stored as Vec<u8> inside the Inode struct. Writes resize the vec; truncate truncates it.
data_model.Directory data: A directory inode maps to a BTreeMap<String, u64> (name → child inode number). BTreeMap gives sorted readdir for free.
data_model.Symlink data: A symlink inode stores a single String target path.
data_model.Extended attributes: Per-inode HashMap<String, Vec<u8>> stored in a parallel BTreeMap<u64, HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>> inside the filesystem container.
data_model.File handle: open/create return a u64 handle that maps to an OpenFileHandle struct tracking the inode number, open flags, and current seek offset. Handles are stored in a slab allocator.

data_structures.name: Inode
data_structures.description: Core inode metadata and data container. One per filesystem object (file, directory, symlink).
fields: ino: u64 — unique inode number
mode: u32 — file type + permission bits (S_IFREG | S_IFDIR | S_IFLNK | perm)
uid: u32 — owner user id
gid: u32 — owning group id
size: u64 — logical file size in bytes
nlink: u32 — hard link count (dirs count self+children entries; not used for hardlinks since feature is disabled)
atime: Duration — last access time
mtime: Duration — last modification time
ctime: Duration — last status change time
data: InodeData — union of File(Vec<u8>), Directory, or Symlink(String)

data_structures.name: OpenFileHandle
data_structures.description: Tracks an open file's state: which inode, access flags, and current read/write cursor position.
fields: fh: u64 — file handle id (index into slab)
ino: u64 — inode this handle refers to
flags: i32 — O_RDONLY / O_WRONLY / O_RDWR / O_APPEND etc.
offset: u64 — current seek position for read/write

data_structures.name: Filesystem
data_structures.description: Top-level filesystem state. Single instance wrapped in RwLock<Filesystem>.
fields: inodes: BTreeMap<u64, Inode> — all live inodes keyed by inode number
next_ino: u64 — next unused inode number
dirs: BTreeMap<u64, BTreeMap<String, u64>> — directory entries per directory inode
xattrs: BTreeMap<u64, HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>> — extended attributes per inode
handles: Slab<OpenFileHandle> — slab-allocated open file handles
uid: u32 — mount-time caller uid
gid: u32 — mount-time caller gid

data_structures.name: InodeData
data_structures.description: Enum covering the three supported inode types. Keeps memory compact.
fields: File(Vec<u8>) — raw byte buffer for regular files
Directory — unit variant; child entries stored in Filesystem.dirs
Symlink(String) — target path string

data_structures.name: StatFs
data_structures.description: Canonical representation of statfs/statvfs data returned to the kernel.
fields: blocks: u64
bfree: u64
bavail: u64
files: u64
ffree: u64
bsize: u32
namemax: u32

api_boundaries: main → filesystem: mount options → Filesystem::new(); then pass &Filesystem to FUSE session.
filesystem → inode: inode_alloc(mode, uid, gid) → u64; get_inode(ino) → &Inode; write_data(ino, offset, buf); truncate(ino, size).
filesystem → directory: add_entry(dir_ino, name, child_ino); remove_entry(dir_ino, name); lookup(dir_ino, name) → Option<u64>; list_entries(dir_ino) → Vec<(String, u64)>.
filesystem → xattr: get_xattr(ino, key); set_xattr(ino, key, val); list_xattr(ino); remove_xattr(ino, key).
filesystem → symlink: create_symlink(ino, target) → u64; read_link(ino) → String.
filesystem → permissions: can_read(inode, uid, gid) → bool; can_write(inode, uid, gid) → bool; can_execute(inode, uid, gid) → bool; can_search_dir(dir_ino, uid, gid) → bool.
filesystem → path: resolve(path) → Option<u64>; resolve_parent(path) → Option<(u64, String)>; validate_name(name) → Result<()>.
All FUSE op callbacks get &RwLock<Filesystem>; acquire read lock for queries, write lock for mutations.
limitations: No persistence — all data lost on unmount.
Hard links not supported (nlink is maintained for directory accounting only).
Inode numbers are never recycled (monotonic counter).
No access control lists (ACLs), only traditional Unix rwx bits.
No extended attribute namespace enforcement beyond basic prefix checks (user.*, trusted.*, security.*).
Maximum file size limited by available memory (Vec<u8>).
No rename across different parent directories with atomic guarantees beyond lock-held scope.
memory_management: arena/boxed allocation; Drop-based cleanup on unmount; all inodes freed when filesystem goes out of scope
error_handling: errno-based via libc::E* constants; each FUSE op returns c_int with negated errno on failure
